findings.title: [P1] Non-finite values bypass validation and return NaN/Infinity instead of throwing
findings.body: With `Number(value)`, any non-numeric or partially-numeric string coerces to `NaN` (`"abc"`, `"12abc"`), and `"Infinity"` coerces to `Infinity`. The new guard `Number.isFinite(timeout) && (...)` evaluates false for these, so the `throw new Error("invalid timeout")` is skipped and the non-finite value is returned. Previously these inputs threw: `parseInt("abc")` was `NaN`, and `!Number.isSafeInteger(NaN)` was true. The function's sole contract — reject invalid timeouts — is now silently disabled for the most common misconfiguration class: a caller passing a garbage config value gets `NaN` back with no error, which then propagates into timing logic (e.g., `setTimeout(fn, NaN)` fires after ~1 ms in Node). The guard direction is inverted; it should reject non-finite values (e.g., `!Number.isFinite(timeout) || (...)`). Confirmed against `src/options.ts`: `parseTimeout` is exported with no other in-repo callers, so its validation/error contract is the API being changed, and the PR description explicitly claims contracts are preserved.
